_comment: Hard limits (design §7). MCP rules match the tool's own name, the part after the last '__', lowercased, for any server prefix. Order: money deny, outbound deny (drafts exempt), create allow, then ask. A rule's optional "input" reads the tool's arguments: keys are compared lowercased with everything but letters and digits removed, by suffix (conflict_behavior, conflictBehavior and @microsoft.graph.conflictBehavior all end in conflictbehavior); "allow" must match every such value; "when_missing" decides when no such key is given. Regexes are Python syntax.

mcp._private_publish: Full tool names exempt from the outbound rule: claude.ai artifacts are created private to the CEO and these tools can't share them (the dashboard skill uses them). Commenting and sharing stay outbound.

deny.why: moving money, refunds and invoice issuing happen in the vendor's own UI, by the CEO (hard limit 2); reading payments, transfers and invoices is fine
outbound is draft-only: agents draft, the CEO sends (hard limit 1). Create a draft instead

create.why: uploads a new file: on a name clash it fails or picks a new name, so nothing is lost
creates a folder; the servers fail or rename on a name clash
copies to a new item; the servers fail on a name clash at the destination

mcp._create: Creating can't lose anything, so it doesn't ask (hard limit 4, three classes, decided 2026-11-11). An upload counts as creating only if it explicitly sets its conflict behaviour to fail or rename: defaults differ by server.

ask.why: may overwrite an existing document: the CEO confirms (hard limit 4). Uploads, copies and new folders that set their conflict behaviour to fail or rename only create, and don't ask
deletes, moves or renames documents or mail: the CEO confirms (hard limit 4)

_known_prefixes: Servers whose tool names the hard limits were checked against. Each one's outbound tools are also denied in the settings template's permission rules, as a second layer; a server with no outbound tools (m365-mail: drafts, moves and deletes only) has nothing to deny there.

deny.why: force push rewrites shared history (hard limit 4)
